findings.claim: A team with an authorized fallback on a different provider is rejected during capture because the fallback retains the primary resolved_provider_id.
findings.evidence: The Some(profile) branch clones primary config, changes model/api_key/base_url at lines 316–319, then apply_credential_decision checks resolved_provider_id before the model prefix (lines 30–36). Manager lines 5368–5389 creates the fallback decision with Orchestrator::fallback_llm_config, which clears resolved_provider_id (src/llm/orchestrator.rs:1552), so that decision has the fallback provider. A primary openai resolved identity and authorized anthropic fallback therefore compare unequal. The ? at line 321 aborts whole-run capture before fallback or primary execution. The current team adapter at scripts/release/uar_1_1_1_runtime.py:620 exercises one provider and does not cover this branch.
findings.reproducer: Unexecuted reproduction: install a team binding with distinct primary and fallback provider IDs and valid endpoint profiles, grant both exact source tuples, and admit a team attempt. Capture reaches line 321 with primary resolved_provider_id and fallback decision provider_id; the run reports TEAM_PROVIDER_REQUEST_REJECTED instead of using the authorized route. Falsifying evidence would be a source step that replaces resolved_provider_id before line 321; none is present.
findings.suggested_fix: Construct the team fallback config with the fallback provider identity (or reuse fallback_llm_config and explicitly bind the endpoint profile's provider), then apply its captured decision. Add the distinct-provider team case to the already selected real integration group.
findings.requirement: tenant-isolation: Credential source authority covers every provider capture; kubo-runtime-conformance: retain accepted Kubo conformance behaviors.

findings.claim: Disabled fallback entries can prevent an otherwise authorized primary run.
findings.evidence: fallback_credential_decisions resolves every entry without testing run_failover_config.enabled. A denied source returns Err at line 5389 and the tuple match propagates it at line 5442. Actual RunModelBindings::capture only uses fallback entries inside if failover.enabled (bindings.rs:292). Thus disabled entries still acquire policy/credential dependencies.
findings.reproducer: Unexecuted reproduction: shared mode, exact grant for the primary config source, failover.enabled=false, and a populated fallback_models entry with a config key but no fallback source grant. Primary capture is refused despite failover being disabled. The same primary succeeds when the inert list is empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve fallback decisions only for the fallback set that can actually be captured, respecting failover.enabled; preserve fail-closed behavior for enabled fallbacks.
findings.requirement: tenant-isolation: exact selected source authority and compatibility deployment.

findings.claim: The acceptance program's log secret-leak assertions cannot detect runtime leaks because logs are redacted before the assertions.
findings.evidence: RuntimeLease.logs returns resources.redact(stdout+stderr) at scripts/release/uar_1_1_1_support.py:169–171. RuntimeLease construction registers config api_key values, so runtime-fixture-key is removed first. The checks at runtime.py:314 and 434 consequently pass even if the raw runtime log contains that key. This does not demonstrate a production leak; it demonstrates that this negative control cannot observe one.
findings.reproducer: Unexecuted falsifying observation: supply a raw runtime log containing runtime-fixture-key through RuntimeLease.logs; it becomes [redacted] before the membership assertion. Both safe and leaking runtime output satisfy the assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Perform leak detection against raw output in memory, then persist only a redacted transcript and safe detection result. Keep raw secrets out of retained evidence and error messages.
findings.requirement: provider-diagnostic-status: diagnostic origin is safe to log; verification.md: required positive/negative observations must be actual installed-artifact evidence.
findings.evidence_kind: static fixture data-flow; no leak or product test executed

findings.claim: The published gate does not establish that the tested image was built from the receipt's source commit.
findings.evidence: inspect_image checks digest membership in the supplied index and OS/architecture, then records image ID. read_manifest checks the local v1.1.1 tag against source_commit at lines 178–180, independently from the supplied image/index. No check links the image to that commit or a publishing workflow run. Receipt lines 196–199 copy the manifest source identity. Documentation asks the operator to record workflow identity separately, so this is an unresolved provenance limit rather than a claim that a wrong image has already passed.
findings.reproducer: Unexecuted falsifying observation: replace image/index_digest with another immutable same-platform build that supports the same tested behavior while keeping source_commit and local tag unchanged. Existing identity checks do not reject the source mismatch. A separately verified publication receipt could close this gap, but none is supplied.
findings.suggested_fix: Before published acceptance is credited, verify and retain a publication receipt linking workflow run/commit, tag source commit, index and both child digests; make the gate bind to that receipt or explicitly require its independent verification in the release disposition.
findings.requirement: kubo-runtime-conformance: patch release claims identify accepted immutable artifacts; verification.md: wrong child/source/platform withholds success.
findings.evidence_kind: static acceptance/provenance review; publication not executed
